text: Zero as a number was developed in India; Brahmagupta gave rules for it in 628 AD.
Pi is irrational: its decimals never end or repeat.
Pi Day is March 14 (3/14), also Albert Einstein's birthday.
Archimedes showed pi is between 3 10/71 and 3 1/7.
The symbol π for pi was popularized by Leonhard Euler in the 1700s.
Euler's identity, e^(iπ) + 1 = 0, links five key constants.
e is about 2.71828 and is the base of natural logarithms.
The golden ratio is about 1.618.
Each Fibonacci number is the sum of the two before it: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13...
Ratios of consecutive Fibonacci numbers approach the golden ratio.
Fibonacci introduced Hindu-Arabic numerals to Europe in his 1202 book Liber Abaci.
There are infinitely many prime numbers, proved by Euclid around 300 BC.
2 is the only even prime number.
1 is not considered a prime number.
The largest known primes are Mersenne primes, of the form 2^p - 1.
A googol is 1 followed by 100 zeros.
The name Google came from 'googol'.
The word 'googol' was coined by 9-year-old Milton Sirotta in 1938.
A googolplex is 1 followed by a googol zeros.
Zero is neither positive nor negative.
Any number to the power 0 equals 1 (except 0, which is debated).
The sum of the angles in a triangle is 180 degrees.
A triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5 is a right triangle.
The Pythagorean theorem: a² + b² = c² for right triangles.
Babylonian tablet Plimpton 322 lists Pythagorean triples about 3,800 years ago.
Fermat's Last Theorem says aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ has no whole-number solutions for n > 2.
Andrew Wiles proved Fermat's Last Theorem in 1994, after 358 years.
Fermat wrote that his margin was too small to contain his proof.
A circle has 360 degrees, a Babylonian tradition.
The Babylonians used a base-60 number system, which gives us 60 minutes and seconds.
The Mayans used a base-20 number system with a symbol for zero.
Roman numerals have no symbol for zero.
In Roman numerals, M is 1,000 and D is 500.
The equals sign was invented by Robert Recorde in 1557.
Recorde chose two parallel lines because 'no two things can be more equal.'
The plus and minus signs first appeared in print in 1489.
The word 'algebra' comes from the Arabic 'al-jabr', from al-Khwarizmi's 9th-century book.
The word 'algorithm' comes from the name al-Khwarizmi.
A 'dozen' is 12 and a 'gross' is 144.
A 'baker's dozen' is 13.
The number 1729 is the smallest number expressible as the sum of two cubes in two ways.
1729 is called the Hardy–Ramanujan number, after a taxi ride story.
Srinivasa Ramanujan was largely self-taught and filled notebooks with discoveries.
A perfect number equals the sum of its divisors: 6 = 1 + 2 + 3.
28 is the second perfect number: 1 + 2 + 4 + 7 + 14.
All known perfect numbers are even.
Nobody knows whether an odd perfect number exists.
Goldbach's conjecture says every even number above 2 is the sum of two primes; still unproven.
The twin prime conjecture asks if there are infinitely many primes 2 apart.
The Riemann Hypothesis carries a $1 million Millennium Prize.
The Poincaré conjecture was proved by Grigori Perelman, who declined the $1 million prize.
There are seven Millennium Prize Problems; only one has been solved.
The Fields Medal is awarded every four years to mathematicians under 40.
Maryam Mirzakhani was the first woman to win the Fields Medal, in 2014.
There is no Nobel Prize in mathematics.
The Abel Prize, first given in 2003, is often called math's Nobel.
A Möbius strip has only one side and one edge.
A Klein bottle has no inside or outside.
To a topologist, a coffee cup and a donut are the same shape.
The Four Color Theorem: any map needs at most four colors.
The Four Color Theorem (1976) was the first major proof done with a computer.
Euler solved the Seven Bridges of Königsberg problem in 1736, founding graph theory.
There are exactly five Platonic solids.
A soccer ball pattern is a truncated icosahedron: 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons.
Bees build hexagonal cells, which use the least wax for the area.
Honeycomb efficiency was proved mathematically by Thomas Hales in 1999.
A sphere has the smallest surface area for its volume.
Archimedes asked that a sphere inside a cylinder be carved on his tomb.
A sphere's volume is two-thirds that of the cylinder around it.
Eratosthenes estimated Earth's circumference around 240 BC using shadows.
The Rhind Papyrus, about 1550 BC, is an Egyptian math textbook.
Hypatia of Alexandria was a renowned mathematician around 400 AD.
Euclid's Elements was used as a textbook for over 2,000 years.
Leonhard Euler kept producing mathematics after going nearly blind.
Euler is among the most prolific mathematicians, with over 800 papers and books.
Carl Friedrich Gauss is called the 'Prince of Mathematicians'.
As a child, Gauss reportedly added 1 to 100 quickly: the answer is 5,050.
The sum of 1 to n is n(n+1)/2.
Isaac Newton and Gottfried Leibniz independently invented calculus.
Leibniz's notation, like dx and the ∫ sign, is the one we use today.
The ∫ symbol is a stretched 'S' for 'sum'.
Newton was also Warden of the Royal Mint.
René Descartes invented the coordinate system, named 'Cartesian' after him.
Blaise Pascal built a mechanical calculator at age 19.
Pascal's triangle was known in China and Persia centuries before Pascal.
Ada Lovelace wrote what is considered the first computer program, in 1843.
Ada Lovelace was the daughter of the poet Lord Byron.
Alan Turing helped break the Enigma code in World War II.
Alan Turing appears on the Bank of England's £50 note.
Katherine Johnson calculated trajectories for NASA's early spaceflights.
John Glenn asked for Katherine Johnson to check the computer's numbers before his orbit.
Emmy Noether's theorem links symmetry to conservation laws in physics.
Sophie Germain wrote to Gauss under a man's name, 'Monsieur LeBlanc'.
Lewis Carroll, author of Alice in Wonderland, was a mathematician at Oxford.
Probability theory began with letters between Pascal and Fermat in 1654.
In a room of 23 people, there's over a 50% chance two share a birthday.
With 70 people, a shared birthday is over 99.9% likely.
The Monty Hall problem: switching doors gives a 2/3 chance of winning.
A shuffled deck is almost certainly in an order never seen before: 52! is about 8 × 10⁶⁷.
There are 2,598,960 possible five-card poker hands.
The odds of a royal flush are about 1 in 649,740.
Rolling two dice, 7 is the most likely total.
Opposite faces of a standard die add to 7.
A Rubik's Cube has about 43 quintillion positions.
Any Rubik's Cube position can be solved in 20 moves or fewer.
Chess has more possible games than atoms in the observable universe, by Shannon's estimate.
The wheat-and-chessboard puzzle: doubling grains on 64 squares gives over 18 quintillion.
Folding paper in half doubles thickness; 42 folds would reach past the Moon.
A number is divisible by 3 if its digits add to a multiple of 3.
A number is divisible by 9 if its digits add to a multiple of 9.
A number is divisible by 11 if alternating digit sums differ by a multiple of 11.
Multiplying any number by 9 gives digits that add to a multiple of 9.
142857 × 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 gives the same digits rearranged.
1/7 = 0.142857 repeating.
1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3 = 1, so 0.999... repeating equals 1.
The square root of 2 was the first number known to be irrational.
Legend says a Pythagorean was drowned for revealing √2 is irrational.
A 'palindrome number' reads the same backward, like 12321.
The year 2002 was a palindrome year.
Squaring numbers made of 1s gives palindromes: 11² = 121, 111² = 12321.
A 'prime gap' can be as large as you like.
The ancient Greeks didn't consider 1 a number at all.
Kepler discovered planets move in ellipses.
The bell curve is also called the normal or Gaussian distribution.
Benford's Law: in many datasets, about 30% of numbers start with the digit 1.
The 'golden angle' of about 137.5° appears in sunflower seed spirals.
Sunflower spirals often come in Fibonacci numbers like 34 and 55.
A circle's area is π times the radius squared.
A circle's circumference is π times its diameter.
Pi has been calculated to over 100 trillion digits.
NASA uses only about 15 digits of pi for interplanetary navigation.
Indiana's 1897 'Pi Bill' nearly declared a wrong value of pi by law.
Tau (τ) is 2π, about 6.283.
Infinity comes in different sizes, shown by Georg Cantor.
There are as many even numbers as whole numbers.
There are more real numbers than whole numbers.
Hilbert's Hotel is a puzzle showing a full infinite hotel can still take new guests.
David Hilbert posed 23 famous problems in 1900.
Kurt Gödel proved some true statements can never be proved.
The abacus is one of the oldest calculating tools, used for thousands of years.
John Napier invented logarithms in 1614.
The slide rule, based on logarithms, was used for 350 years until calculators.
The Apollo astronauts carried slide rules as backups.
The first handheld electronic calculators appeared around 1970.
'Percent' means 'per hundred'.
A 'billion' is a thousand million in the US system.
A 'myriad' was the Greek word for 10,000.
The 'Rule of 72': divide 72 by an interest rate to estimate years to double money.
Compound interest is how e was discovered, by Jacob Bernoulli.
The Bernoulli family produced eight notable mathematicians.
Every number can be written as a sum of four squares (Lagrange, 1770).
Fermat proved some primes are sums of two squares: 13 = 4 + 9.
A 'magic square' has rows, columns and diagonals with the same sum.
The Lo Shu square from ancient China is a 3×3 magic square summing to 15.
Albrecht Dürer's engraving Melencolia I contains a 4×4 magic square showing the year 1514.
Sudoku puzzles have 6.67 × 10²¹ possible filled grids.
A Sudoku needs at least 17 clues to have a unique solution.
The word 'geometry' means 'earth measurement' in Greek.
'Mathematics' comes from the Greek 'mathema', meaning learning.
A 'hexagon' has 6 sides; a 'heptagon' 7; an 'octagon' 8.
A shape with 1,000 sides is a chiliagon.
Stop signs are regular octagons.
The number 4 is considered unlucky in China because it sounds like 'death'.
The number 8 is lucky in China; the 2008 Beijing Olympics opened at 8:08 pm on 8/8/08.
Friday the 13th happens at least once every year.
A leap year is divisible by 4, except century years not divisible by 400.
The year 2000 was a leap year; 1900 was not.
The Gregorian calendar repeats exactly every 400 years.
The 13th of the month is slightly more likely to be a Friday than any other day.
A week of 7 days dates back to ancient Babylon.
A 'fortnight' is 14 days.
The Fibonacci sequence appears in pinecones, pineapples and artichokes.
Nautilus shells are often said to follow the golden ratio, but measurements show they don't exactly.
A fractal looks similar at every scale.
Benoit Mandelbrot coined the word 'fractal' in 1975.
The coastline of Britain has no fixed length; it depends on your ruler.
The Koch snowflake has infinite perimeter but finite area.
Snowflakes have sixfold symmetry.
Penrose tilings cover a plane without ever repeating.
In 2023, the 'hat' tile was found: one shape that tiles the plane without repeating.
Escher's art drew on hyperbolic geometry and tessellations.
The Great Pyramid's base is very nearly a perfect square.
Stonehenge's alignments track the solstices.
Mathematician John Nash's life inspired the film A Beautiful Mind.
Paul Erdős wrote around 1,500 papers with over 500 coauthors.
An 'Erdős number' measures how close you are to Erdős by coauthorship.
Erdős lived out of a suitcase, staying with colleagues.
Terence Tao began university-level math classes at age 9.
Grace Hopper popularized the term 'bug' after finding a moth in a computer.
Binary uses only 0 and 1.
Leibniz studied binary numbers in 1703.
George Boole's logic of true and false underlies all computers.
A 'byte' is 8 bits.
In binary, 10 means two.
There are 10 kinds of people: those who understand binary and those who don't.
A 'nonillion' has 30 zeros in the US system.
Light travels about 186,000 miles per second.
A light-year is about 5.9 trillion miles.
The Earth is about 93 million miles from the Sun.
The Moon is about 239,000 miles from Earth on average.
The Moon's diameter is about 27% of Earth's.
By coincidence, the Sun is about 400 times wider and 400 times farther than the Moon.
That 400 coincidence is why total solar eclipses look so perfect.
A 'square number' is a number times itself: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25...
A 'triangular number' can form a triangle of dots: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15...
Adding two consecutive triangular numbers gives a square number.
The sum of the first n odd numbers is n²: 1 + 3 + 5 = 9.
Every cube is the difference of two squares of triangular numbers.
Nicomachus noticed sums of cubes are squares, around 100 AD.
Ten is the base of our number system, likely because we have ten fingers.
The Yuki people of California counted in base 8 using spaces between fingers.
A 'score' is 20; Lincoln's 'four score and seven' means 87.
Euler's formula for polyhedra: vertices − edges + faces = 2.
A cube has 8 vertices, 12 edges and 6 faces.
A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces.
An icosahedron has 20 faces; d20 dice are icosahedra.
Kepler once modeled the solar system with nested Platonic solids.
The Fibonacci sequence was known in India centuries earlier, in poetry rhythms.
The 'Ishango bone' from Africa, over 20,000 years old, may be an early tally.
The Lebombo bone, about 43,000 years old, has 29 notches.
Mathematician Emmy Noether was called 'the most significant woman in math history' by Einstein.
Florence Nightingale was a pioneering statistician and invented a type of pie chart.
William Playfair invented the bar chart and line graph in the 1780s.
Thomas Jefferson was an enthusiastic amateur mathematician.
President James Garfield published his own proof of the Pythagorean theorem in 1876.
There are over 300 known proofs of the Pythagorean theorem.
Napoleon was a keen mathematician; Napoleon's theorem bears his name.
Isaac Newton's Principia was published in 1687.
Galileo said the book of nature is written in the language of mathematics.
'QED' means 'quod erat demonstrandum': which was to be shown.
The □ symbol at the end of a proof is called the 'tombstone' or 'Halmos'.
A 'lemma' is a stepping-stone theorem.
A 'corollary' follows directly from a theorem.
'Conjecture' means a statement believed but not yet proved.
A 'hypotenuse' is the longest side of a right triangle.
'Isosceles' means 'equal legs' in Greek.
A 'scalene' triangle has no equal sides.
An 'obtuse' angle is more than 90°.
An 'acute' angle is less than 90°.
A 'reflex' angle is more than 180°.
'Sine' comes from a Latin mistranslation of an Arabic word meaning 'bosom' or 'fold'.
Trigonometry means 'triangle measurement'.
Hipparchus made the first known table of chords around 140 BC.
A 'radian' is the angle where the arc equals the radius.
There are about 57.3 degrees in a radian.
A full turn is 2π radians.
A parabola is the path of a thrown ball, ignoring air.
Satellite dishes are parabolic so signals focus at one point.
An ellipse has two foci.
Whispering galleries use ellipses: a whisper at one focus is heard at the other.
The US Capitol's Statuary Hall is a famous whispering gallery.
The catenary curve is the shape of a hanging chain.
The Gateway Arch in St Louis is a flattened catenary.
Gaudí used hanging chains to design his churches upside down.
A cycloid is the curve of a point on a rolling wheel.
A ball rolls fastest down a cycloid ramp, the 'brachistochrone' problem.
The Fibonacci number F(12) = 144 is also a square.
The only square Fibonacci numbers are 0, 1 and 144.
Cicadas emerge in prime-number cycles of 13 or 17 years.
Prime cycles may help cicadas avoid predators with shorter cycles.
Modern internet encryption relies on the difficulty of factoring large numbers.
RSA encryption, invented in 1977, is based on prime numbers.
The 'Caesar cipher' shifts each letter by a fixed amount.
Mary, Queen of Scots, was convicted partly through decoded cipher letters.
Bletchley Park's codebreakers included many women mathematicians.
The Navajo Code Talkers used language, not math, to create an unbroken code.
A 'perfect shuffle' of a deck returns it to order after 8 shuffles.
Seven riffle shuffles are needed to randomize a deck, per Bayer and Diaconis.
The 'law of large numbers': averages settle down with more trials.
The 'gambler's fallacy' is believing past coin flips affect the next.
A fair coin has a 50% chance each flip, no matter what came before.
Real coin tosses slightly favor the side facing up at the start, per Persi Diaconis.
The 'Kissing number' in 3D is 12 spheres touching one sphere.
Kepler conjectured the densest way to stack oranges; it was proved in 1998.
Oranges stacked in a pyramid fill about 74% of the space.
The 'Bridges of Königsberg' have no route crossing each bridge exactly once.
The 'traveling salesman problem' asks for the shortest route visiting every city.
Six degrees of separation suggests everyone is linked by about six acquaintances.
A 'Venn diagram' was introduced by John Venn in 1880.
Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine, a mechanical computer.
The Difference Engine No. 2 was built from Babbage's plans in 1991, and it works.
The ENIAC, finished in 1945, weighed about 30 tons.
NASA's 'human computers' did calculations by hand before electronic computers.
Archimedes said: 'Give me a place to stand and I will move the Earth.'
'Eureka!' means 'I have found it!', attributed to Archimedes.
Archimedes was killed during the Roman siege of Syracuse in 212 BC.
Pythagoras's followers believed 'all is number'.
The Pythagoreans linked musical harmony to whole-number ratios.
An octave doubles a note's frequency, a 2:1 ratio.
A perfect fifth in music is a 3:2 ratio.
Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier explored tuning systems that work in all keys.
Equal temperament divides an octave into 12 equal steps.
Each semitone in equal temperament multiplies frequency by the 12th root of 2.
The 'Mozart effect' on intelligence is not well supported by research.
Tom Lehrer, satirical songwriter, taught math at MIT and Harvard.
Brian May of Queen holds a PhD in astrophysics.
A 'hendecagon' has 11 sides.
Origami has helped design folding solar panels for space.
Ancient Egyptians wrote fractions as sums of unit fractions like 1/2 + 1/4.
Greek mathematician Diophantus is called the 'father of algebra'.
A riddle says Diophantus lived to 84.
Omar Khayyam, the poet, was also a mathematician and astronomer.
Khayyam helped reform the Persian calendar to be very accurate.
Indian mathematician Aryabhata estimated pi as 3.1416 around 499 AD.
Madhava of India found infinite series for pi in the 1300s.
Chinese mathematician Zu Chongzhi found pi ≈ 355/113 around 480 AD.
355/113 matches pi to six decimal places.
'22/7' is a common approximation of pi, accurate to two decimals.
Pi Approximation Day is July 22 (22/7).
'Mole Day' is October 23, from 6.02 × 10²³.
Fibonacci Day is November 23 (1, 1, 2, 3).
Square Root Day happens when day and month are the square root of the year's last digits, like 4/4/16.
The Collatz conjecture says repeatedly halving evens and tripling-plus-one odds always reaches 1; it's unproven.
Square Root Days include 3/3/09, 4/4/16 and 5/5/25; the next is 6/6/36.
6 is the smallest perfect number.
9 times any digit gives digits summing to 9, like 9 × 7 = 63.
12 has more divisors than any smaller number.
23 is the number of people for the birthday paradox to pass 50%.
24 is 4 factorial: 4 × 3 × 2 × 1.
27 is 3 cubed.
42 is the 'answer to everything' in The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.
64 is both a square (8²) and a cube (4³).
73 is the 21st prime, and 21 = 7 × 3; 37 is the 12th prime.
89 is a Fibonacci number, and 1/89 hides the Fibonacci sequence in its decimals.
128 is 2 to the 7th power, and our wall is 128 pixels wide.
144 is a 'gross' and 12 squared.
360 has 24 divisors, which is why it's handy for a circle.
496 is the third perfect number.
720 is 6 factorial, the minutes in 12 hours.
1,000 seconds is about 16.7 minutes; a million seconds is about 11.6 days.
A billion seconds is about 31.7 years.
An 81-year life is about 2.56 billion seconds.
The average heart beats about 100,000 times a day.
8,128 is the fourth perfect number.
10! seconds is exactly 6 weeks.
A 'centillion' has 303 zeros in the US system.
Multiplying 1089 by 9 gives 9801, its reverse.
Kaprekar's constant is 6174: sort four digits high-to-low minus low-to-high, and repeat.
Any 3-digit number like 123123 (repeated) is divisible by 7, 11 and 13.
Adding 1 to 2³ gives 3², the only consecutive powers (Catalan, proved 2002).
The number 2 is called 'the oddest prime' as a joke because it is the only even one.
In a group of 367 people, two must share a birthday, by the pigeonhole principle.
London has two people with the same number of hairs on their heads, by the pigeonhole principle.
A 'triskaidekaphobe' fears the number 13.
Many buildings skip a 13th floor label.
A 'gross of grosses' is 1,728, a 'great gross'.
1,728 is 12 cubed, also the cubic inches in a cubic foot.
A cubic foot of water weighs about 62.4 pounds.
A US gallon is exactly 231 cubic inches.
A mile is 5,280 feet.
A nautical mile is based on one minute of latitude.
An acre was originally land a yoke of oxen could plow in a day.
A 'hand', used for horses, is 4 inches.
A 'league' was about the distance a person walks in an hour, roughly 3 miles.
2 to the 10th power is 1,024, which is why a kilobyte is sometimes 1,024 bytes.
There are 17 distinct wallpaper symmetry groups for repeating flat patterns.
Forty is the only English number name with its letters in alphabetical order.
The digits of 1/81 run 0.012345679 repeating, skipping 8.
Every whole number greater than 1 factors into primes in exactly one way.
A hexagon's side equals the radius of the circle around it.
The angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360 degrees.
